title: The testing pyramid applied to the front-end

videos.script:
This course asks three questions of a finished screen. {{three}} Does it work? Can it be trusted with somebody's data? And can everybody use it?

You will ask them of one small app, a study planner, and you build it today. {{planner}} It lists your courses, adds study sessions, and totals your week. It has no framework in it, so every lesson shows the idea and nothing else.

Then the first question gets a shape. {{pyramid}} Tests come in layers. The fast ones at the bottom check one function. The slow ones at the top drive a real browser. {{trophy}} For a front-end, the widest layer is the middle one. That is where the pieces meet, and where screens break.

The bottom layer runs nothing at all. {{types}} The type checker reads every file, and finds a whole kind of mistake for free.

One more thing before you start. {{fails}} Setting up a project is where many people give up. So one section is about what to do when it fails. Read it before you need it.
